title: Finite locally constant sheaves of modules: finite values iff finite stalks
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For an etale morphism $u:U\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] write $\mathcal G|_U$ for the restriction of $\mathcal G$ to the localised site $Y_{\Et}/U=U_{\Et}$ ($V\mapsto\mathcal G(V\to U\to Y)$, a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$); for a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] write $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ for the stalk of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], a $\Lambda$-module by $\lambda\cdot(\text{germ of }s)=\text{germ of }\lambda s$. The following are equivalent: (1) there are an etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ (a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms) and finite $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ (finite as sets) such that $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$, the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules with value $M_i$ on $(U_i)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], for every $i$ (locally constant with finite constant values: the analogue for $\Lambda$-modules of Stacks 03RU, which states 'finite locally constant' for sheaves of sets and of abelian groups only); (2) $\mathcal G$ is finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant] for the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules, i.e. locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant] and finite [def-constructible-finite]: every geometric stalk $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is a finite set; (3) $\mathcal G$ is locally constant and of finite type as a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type] (Stacks 03RW (3), $\Lambda$ being Noetherian as a finite ring). Moreover, in (1), for every $i$ and every geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ factoring through $U_i$ ($\bar y=u_i\circ\bar u$ for a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U_i$) the stalk $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is isomorphic to $M_i$ as a $\Lambda$-module.

proof.text: *Stalks as $\Lambda$-modules.* For a sheaf $\mathcal H$ of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of a scheme $T$ and a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, $\mathcal H_{\bar t}$ is the colimit of the abelian groups $\mathcal H(V)$ over the pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar t$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This index category is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (1), (2), applied with $R=\mathbf Z$ and with $R=\Lambda$, the colimit in abelian groups and the colimit in $\Lambda$-modules are the same set of germs (every element is a germ, two germs agree iff the sections agree on a common refinement), and the $\Lambda$-module structure of the latter is $\lambda\cdot(\text{germ of }s)=\text{germ of }\lambda s$, the structure of the statement. A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H'$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules induces the $\Lambda$-linear map $\varphi_{\bar t}$ (germ of $s$ $\mapsto$ germ of $\varphi(s)$), and an isomorphism induces an isomorphism.

source.place: Definition 040R (definition-stalk) with Lemma 03PQ (cofinal-etale), stalks as filtered colimits

proof.text: *Stalk of a restriction.* Let $u:U\to Y$ be etale, $\bar u$ a geometric point of $U$ and $\bar y=u\circ\bar u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal G$, there is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves $\rho_{\mathcal G}:u^{-1}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G|_U$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], natural in the abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] an isomorphism $c_{u,\bar u,\mathcal G}:(u^{-1}\mathcal G)_{\bar u}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_{\bar y}$, natural in $\mathcal G$. Hence $c_{u,\bar u,\mathcal G}\circ((\rho_{\mathcal G})_{\bar u})^{-1}:(\mathcal G|_U)_{\bar u}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. It is $\Lambda$-linear: for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, multiplication by $\lambda$ is an endomorphism $m_\lambda$ of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$, its restriction $m_\lambda|_U$ is multiplication by $\lambda$ on $\mathcal G|_U$, and by step 1 the induced maps on stalks are multiplication by $\lambda$; naturality of $\rho$ and $c$ with respect to $m_\lambda$ says that the composite commutes with multiplication by $\lambda$.

source.place: Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback: stalks of an inverse image), Section 03PZ (section-inverse-image); the identification of restriction and inverse image along an etale morphism is the cited node; agent-assembled

proof.text: *Stalk of a constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules.* Let $T$ be a scheme, $M$ a $\Lambda$-module, $\underline M$ the constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ with its canonical $\Lambda$-linear map $\iota:(V\mapsto M)\to\underline M$ from the constant presheaf, and $\bar t$ a geometric point of $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-sheaf-underlying] the underlying abelian sheaf of $\underline M$ is the constant abelian sheaf with value $M$, compatibly with the maps from the constant presheaf; so by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] the map $M\to\underline M_{\bar t}$, $m\mapsto$ germ of $\iota_T(m)$ at $(T,\bar t)$, is an isomorphism of abelian groups. It is $\Lambda$-linear, since $\iota_T$ is $\Lambda$-linear and $\lambda\cdot(\text{germ of }s)=\text{germ of }\lambda s$ (step 1). So $\underline M_{\bar t}\cong M$ as $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Section 093I (section-constant): the constant sheaf of Lambda-modules is the constant sheaf with its module structure; Etale Cohomology Lemma 03PT (2) for the stalk

proof.text: *The 'moreover' clause, for any values.* Suppose $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}$ is an etale covering and $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{N_i}$ (constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(U_i)_{\Et}$) for $\Lambda$-modules $N_i$, not necessarily finite. Let $\bar u$ be a geometric point of $U_i$ and $\bar y=u_i\circ\bar u$. Then, as $\Lambda$-modules, $\mathcal G_{\bar y}\cong(\mathcal G|_{U_i})_{\bar u}$ by step 2, $(\mathcal G|_{U_i})_{\bar u}\cong(\underline{N_i})_{\bar u}$ by step 1 (the stalk of the given isomorphism), and $(\underline{N_i})_{\bar u}\cong N_i$ by step 3 with $T=U_i$. In particular, under (1) ($N_i=M_i$) this is the 'moreover' clause.

source.place: Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant), part for Lambda-modules; composition of steps 1-3

proof.text: *(1) implies (2).* Assume (1). Each $\underline{M_i}$ is a constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules in the sense of [def-constructible-constant] (coefficient category the $\Lambda$-modules), so $\{U_i\to Y\}$ is a trivialising datum and $\mathcal G$ is locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Let $\bar y$ be a geometric point of $Y$. Since the $u_i$ are etale and jointly surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] gives $i$ and a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U_i$ with $u_i\circ\bar u=\bar y$; by step 4, $\mathcal G_{\bar y}\cong M_i$ is a finite set. So $\mathcal G$ is finite [def-constructible-finite], hence finite locally constant [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant].

*(2) implies (1).* Assume (2): there are an etale covering $\{u_i:U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ and $\Lambda$-modules $N_i$ with $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{N_i}$ [def-constructible-locally-constant], [def-constructible-constant]. Let $I'=\{i\in I:U_i\neq\emptyset\}$; since an empty $U_i$ has empty image, $\{u_i\}_{i\in I'}$ is still jointly surjective, hence an etale covering. For $i\in I'$ choose a point $x\in U_i$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; the point $x$ with $\kappa(x)\to\Omega$ is a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U_i$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. By step 4, $N_i\cong\mathcal G_{u_i\circ\bar u}$, which is finite by (2) [def-constructible-finite]. So $\{u_i\}_{i\in I'}$ with $M_i=N_i$ satisfies (1).

*(1) implies (3).* Assume (1). By step 5, $\mathcal G$ is locally constant. Each $M_i$ is finite, so it is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module (generated by its finitely many elements) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-values-finite-type], applied to the covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ and the isomorphisms $\mathcal G|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}$, $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-etale-module-finite-type].

*(3) implies (2).* Assume (3). $\mathcal G$ is locally constant by assumption. Let $\bar y$ be a geometric point of $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-sheaf-stalk-finitely-generated], $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module, say generated by $x_1,\dots,x_n$; then $\Lambda^n\to\mathcal G_{\bar y}$, $(\lambda_j)\mapsto\sum_j\lambda_jx_j$, is surjective, so $\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ has at most $|\Lambda|^n<\infty$ elements, $\Lambda$ being finite. So $\mathcal G$ is finite [def-constructible-finite] and locally constant, i.e. (2) [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant].
